pillars.title: AI & Machine Learning
pillars.summary: How intelligent systems are actually built: data, training, evaluation, and the honest limits of what a model can do — practiced on low-resource Khmer problems where shortcuts fail fast.
pillars.groundedIn: Computer Science coursework at Fort Hays State and the Kaskor ASR fine-tuning pipeline.

pillars.title: Software & Product Systems
pillars.summary: Turning models and ideas into systems people can use: applications, workflows, APIs, architecture, and the deployment discipline that keeps them dependable.
pillars.groundedIn: Information Technology Management coursework at AUPP and product work with CHNAI LAB.

pillars.title: Business & Strategy
pillars.summary: Whether a system is worth building: user needs, unit economics, operations, and the market reality that decides if something useful is also commercially viable.
pillars.groundedIn: International business studies and field validation for Chomkar OrderLoop in Kampong Cham.

pillars.title: Governance & Commercial Rules
pillars.summary: What a system is allowed — and ought — to do: contracts, terms, policies, privacy, risk, and the human-approval points that keep consequential decisions accountable.
topics: Contracts, terms, and policies for AI products
pillars.groundedIn: Contracts, terms, and policy work in my international business studies, plus the human-approval and audit patterns built into Chomkar Decision Grid.

connection: These are not four separate interests. The CS and ITM degrees build the ability to make intelligent systems; the international business studies and field research supply the commercial lens; and the contracts, terms, and policy work asks what those systems are allowed — and ought — to do. Every project on this site touches at least two pillars, on purpose.
